Please read the following multiple-choice questions and provide the most likely correct answer based on the options given.

Context: None

Question: A television picture is composed of approximately 300,000 individual picture elements, each of which can attain ten different and distinguishable brightness levels (such as black and shades of gray) for proper contrast. If, for any picture element, the probability of occurrence of the ten brightness levels are equal, and 30 picture frames are being transmitted per second, determine the bandwidth of the T.V. video signal. Assume that the signal-to-noise ratio of 1000 (30 db) is required for proper reproduction of any picture.

Options: 
A. 2.5MHz
B. 1.5MHz
C. 6MHz
D. 8MHz
E. 2MHz
F. 4MHz
G. 3MHz
H. 1MHz
I. 7MHz
J. 5MHz

Provide the correct letter choice in \boxed{X}, where X is the correct letter choice. Keep the explanation or feedback within 3 sentences.

Using an equal probability distribution for the brightness levels, the information content per pixel is $\log_2(10)$ bits.

First, calculate the total bit rate ($R$):
$$R = \text{Pixels/frame} \times \text{Frame rate/sec} \times \text{Bits per pixel}$$
$$R = 300,000 \times 30 \times \log_2(10) \approx 9,000,000 \times 3.322 \approx 29.9 \text{ Mbps}$$

Next, according to Shannon's Theorem, the maximum channel capacity ($C$) is related to the bandwidth ($B$) and the signal-to-noise ratio ($SNR$ linear ratio = 1000):
$$C = B \log_2(1 + SNR)$$
$$B = \frac{R}{\log_2(1 + 1000)} \approx \frac{30 \times 10^6}{\log_2(1001)} \approx \frac{30 \times 10^6}{10} = 3 \times 10^6 \text{ Hz}$$

This corresponds to 3 MHz.
